newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN says 7.6 million babies die each year.
newsitem.headline: UN says 7.6 million babies die each year.

text.p: More than 7.6 million babies die each year in late pregnancy, birth or the first week of life -- nearly three out of four of them in south-central Asia and Africa, according to World Health Organisation (WHO) figures released on Friday.
Giving figures for "perinatal" deaths, the U.N. agency said newborn children were neglected in many poor countries and action by the authorities to prevent infant mortality was of a low priority.

Of the 7.6 million perinatal deaths each year, 3.4 million were of children in the first week of life and the rest occurred in late pregnancy and birth, according to the WHO's weekly epidemiological record.
"Almost 40 per cent of estimated perinatal deaths take place in south-central Asia, where 30 per cent of the world's births occur," it said.
Nearly one-third of perinatal deaths occurred in Africa, which has the highest estimated mortality rate of 75 per 1,000 births, it added.
The agency said there were an estimated 140.7 million live births in the world last year.
